issues.legal_issue: Bhumidhari rights created after an Encumbered Estates Act decree may be attached and sold to satisfy that decree when the decree concerns the same property and no law bars execution against those rights.
material_facts: The creditors obtained a simple money decree under the Encumbered Estates Act, which extinguished their former mortgage rights.
The decree and report to the executing authority identified the property liable to attachment and sale, although they could not identify bhumidhari rights that did not yet exist.
After the estate vested in the State, the debtors’ successors acquired new bhumidhari rights in the land.
The Abolition Act contained no prohibition against executing the decree against those rights.
issues.conclusion: The creditors were entitled to proceed against and sell the bhumidhari rights in execution of the decree.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 14(7) and 14(8) of the U.P. Encumbered Estates Act, the decree was a simple money decree executable only under that Act; sections 18, 19(2)(b) and 24 extinguished the former mortgage rights and permitted recovery from the debtor’s property other than proprietary rights in land that the Special Judge had reported as liable to attachment or sale. The nature and extent of the property, rather than the debtor’s particular interest in it, had to be reported. The bhumidhari rights were new rights created under section 18 of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act after the former proprietary interests had vested in the State under sections 4 and 6, and were not themselves proprietary rights. Rana Sheo Ambar Singh v. Allahabad Bank Ltd. was followed as to the new character of bhumidhari rights; its restriction on mortgagees proceeding against those rights did not govern holders of simple money decrees under the Encumbered Estates Act. Krishna Prasad v. Guari Kumari Devi and Shivashankar Prasad Sah v. Baikunth Nath Singh concerned mortgagee remedies under other land-reform statutes and did not determine this issue.

rule.if: encumbered_estate_execution and simple_money_decree and property_within_reported_description and rights_created_after_decree and former_proprietary_interests_vested_in_state and rights_are_nonproprietary and no_law_bars_execution

predicates.encumbered_estate_execution: A creditor sought execution through the statutory process for liquidating an encumbered estate.
predicates.simple_money_decree: The creditor held a simple money decree rather than an enforceable mortgage decree.
predicates.property_within_reported_description: The property against which execution was sought was within the nature and extent of the property identified as liable to attachment or sale.
predicates.rights_created_after_decree: The debtor or successor acquired the rights after the decree was made.
predicates.former_proprietary_interests_vested_in_s: The former proprietor’s interests in the land vested in the State before the debtor or successor acquired the rights at issue.
predicates.rights_are_nonproprietary: The rights at issue were newly created rights and were not the former proprietor’s proprietary rights in the land.
predicates.no_law_bars_execution: No applicable law prohibited execution against the rights at issue.

issues.definition: When a creditor executes a simple money decree through the encumbered-estate process against property already described as liable for execution, newly created nonproprietary rights in that property may be sold if the former proprietary interests have vested in the State and no law bars execution.

issues.legal_issue: Trees constituting a grove that remain the debtor’s property may be attached and sold to satisfy an Encumbered Estates Act decree.
material_facts: The amended decree referred to trees standing on the scheduled lands.
The debtors’ successors possessed the trees when the creditors sought execution.
The trees constituting a grove were excluded from the category of trees that vested in the State; alternatively, any bhumidhari rights over the trees could be proceeded against.
issues.conclusion: The creditors were entitled to proceed against and sell the trees constituting the grove in execution of the decree.
issues.legal_principle: Section 24 of the U.P. Encumbered Estates Act permits execution against the debtor’s property other than proprietary rights in land. Section 3(26) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act adopts the relevant meanings in the U.P. Tenancy Act, and section 3(6) of that Act distinguishes grove land from the trees that constitute a grove. Under section 6(a) of the Abolition Act, trees constituting a grove are excluded from the trees whose rights, title and interest vest in the State. Those trees therefore remain the debtor’s property and may be proceeded against under section 24; alternatively, any bhumidhari rights in them may be executed against under the principle applied to such rights in this judgment, following Rana Sheo Ambar Singh v. Allahabad Bank Ltd.

rule.if: encumbered_estate_execution and trees_identified_in_decree and ((trees_constituted_grove and trees_remained_with_debtor) or trees_subject_to_bhumidhari_rights)

predicates.encumbered_estate_execution: A creditor sought execution through the statutory process for liquidating an encumbered estate.
predicates.trees_identified_in_decree: The decree identified the property on which the trees stood or otherwise included the trees among the property liable for execution.
predicates.trees_constituted_grove: The trees on the land constituted a grove.
predicates.trees_remained_with_debtor: The trees did not vest in the State and remained the debtor’s property.
predicates.trees_subject_to_bhumidhari_rights: The debtor or successor held bhumidhari rights over the trees.

issues.definition: In an encumbered-estate execution, trees identified in the decree may be sold if they constituted a grove and remained with the debtor, or if they were subject to bhumidhari rights.
